subject: Embedder + Streaming function-call fit — decision briefing & next steps
messages:
From: Lila Morgan <lila@medtechco.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: MedTech Co Procurement <procurement@medtechco.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up + pilot ask after demo — triage/triage-rerank use case

Jordan — thanks for the demo earlier. Quick follow-up from our side to make sure we captured everything and surface a few asks for procurement/engineering as we consider a pilot. High level: we liked the streaming demo and the embed + rerank flow, but we need confidence your runtime can deliver predictable latency and structured outputs that map directly into our EHR fields.

Recap of pain points we mentioned:
- Current triage pipeline returns inconsistent top-1 suggestions; clinicians lose trust.
- Reranking is too slow at scale (tail latency spikes during business hours).
- We need output to be structured (JSON with fixed keys) so it can populate EHR fields without manual parsing.
- Cost sensitivity: roughly ~50k inference calls/week for pilot; lower token costs would help justify scale.

Goals for pilot:
- Reduce mean+tail latency for rerank to <250ms for 95th pct under expected load.
- Deliver structured function-call outputs that map to our schema (diagnosis_code, urgency_level, triage_notes).
- Show embedding + rerank improves top-1 accuracy by measurable uplift vs. current BM25 baseline.

Questions / asks:
1) Can you confirm support for streaming function-calls (partial tokens + final JSON assembly) so we can render progress in our UI?
2) Would you propose any SDK changes on our side (client-level streaming helpers, explicit function-call typed responses)?
3) What are the quick wins to lower unit cost (batching, quantization, smaller model fallback)?
4) Procurement asked for an initial ballpark and the SOW so we can start internal approvals.

Attaching a short workflow PDF that shows where we intend to drop the structured output. Happy to hop on a 30m tech sync if that helps.

Thanks,
Lila
Lila Morgan
Head of Product — Clinical AI
MedTech Co

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Lila Morgan <lila@medtechco.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 18:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up + pilot ask after demo — triage/triage-rerank use case

Lila — really appreciate the clear summary. Below is a short decision-briefing style recap and a proposed set of next steps so procurement/eng have something concrete to react to. I copied Priya (solutions) and Ben (tech lead) for the detailed asks.

Short recap (agreed pain/goals):
- Problem: inconsistent top-1 + high rerank latency during peak.
- Goal: streaming-friendly rerank pipeline with structured outputs that map to EHR, and a pilot to validate latency/accuracy improvements.

Technical fit / recommended approach (high level):
- Embed + rerank path: use Redwood embeddings index (dense retrieval) + lightweight reranker model. Index nearest-neighbors on embeddings for candidate generation, then pass candidates to a low-latency transformer reranker.
- Streaming function-call support: Redwood supports chunked streaming where partial tokens can be emitted; we can stream partial reasoning and then emit a final function-call JSON. This is what you saw in the demo.
- Structured outputs: we propose enforcing a JSON schema at the model boundary via function-call spec. The SDK will deserialize into typed objects for you (we'll provide an example mapping to diagnosis_code / urgency_level).
- Cost controls: automatic batching at the gateway, prefix/KV caching for repeated user prompts, and a model-fallback policy (rerank with a cheap quantized model + optional verify pass on a higher-quality model for borderline cases).

SDK changes we recommend on your side:
- Add a streaming client helper (we can supply client snippets) that assembles partial function-call events and validates final schema before committing to EHR.
- Hook for server-side callback on finalized function-call so you can persist and audit the structured payload.
- Optional: integrate our SDK's request-level caching middleware to dedupe similar triage queries during spikes.

Pilot scope (initial):
- Duration: 6 weeks (2-week integration + 4-week data collection)
- Volume: ~50k inference calls/week (as you estimated)
- Success metrics: 95th pct latency <250ms, top-1 accuracy uplift >= 12% vs baseline, validated structured output schema pass rate >= 98%

Next steps we propose:
1) Tech sync (30m) — Priya + Ben + your engineering lead to vet SDK endpoints and the schema (we're available Wed/Thu this week).
2) Draft SOW and ballpark pricing (Ben will attach a draft SOW + a short workbook for procurement).
3) Exchange test account + initial scripts for local validation (we will provide a sandbox key scoped to embeddings/rerank/streaming).

I'm attaching a one-page SOW draft and our SDK change matrix (high level). Ben — can you add a short pricing appendix and send both to Lila/procurement?

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

[attachments: rdw_embedstream_sow_draft.docx, redwood_sdk_change_matrix.xlsx]

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Lila Morgan <lila@medtechco.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Nov 2027 09:31:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up + pilot ask after demo — triage/triage-rerank use case

Lila — quick technical notes from our side to make the tech sync productive. I captured minimal changes required on both sides and an example of what the function-call payload might look like.

1) API surface / endpoints you will use:
- POST /v1/embeddings (bulk support for candidate set construction)
- POST /v1/rerank (streaming supported; returns function-call events)
- GET /v1/model-metrics/{model} (to verify expected latency profile for given sequence length)

2) Auth / rate limits:
- Sandbox tokens will be scoped and rate-limited; pilot keys have tiered burst allowances to emulate production spikes.

3) Example function-call schema (final payload we intend to emit):
{
  "diagnosis_code": "string",
  "urgency_level": "low|medium|high",
  "triage_notes": "string (max 800 chars)",
  "confidence": "float (0-1)",
  "candidate_ids": ["string"]
}

SDK changes / client helpers we will deliver (in the repo / PR):
- streaming-client.js: helper that consumes streaming chunks, validates intermediate partials (so you can render UI), and assembles final JSON on onComplete. Example usage will be included.
- typed-bindings.go (optional): strongly-typed wrapper for your backend to parse function-call responses and reject invalid schema.
- caching-middleware: small middleware to dedupe identical embedding requests (configurable TTL).

4) Performance notes / quick wins:
- We'll recommend a 64-bit vector index shard per 250k vectors to avoid IO hotspots.
- Use quantized 8-bit reranker for candidates <= 5; fallback verify pass only for low-confidence cases to keep cost down.

I can demo the SDK snippets in the tech sync. Jordan — suggest we include a one-page sequence diagram in the meeting so procurement/arch can visualize where keys/PII remain in your VPC.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Natarajan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
